summary: Pema Wangdi is a linguist and Tibetologist who earned a PhD at James Cook University (2017–2021). His career includes posts at the Dzongkha Development Commission (2014–2016) and Central Queensland University as Adjunct Research Fellow (2023).
Peng Zhou works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed a Bachelor of Philosophy at Hunan Normal University (2013–2017) and a Master of Philosophy at Shaanxi Normal University (2017–2020).

Penghao Sun is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied under doctoral supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp, as well as Mark Elliott, Charles Hallisey, Jay Jasanoff, Weirong Shen, and Qingying Chen (2009–2011), among others.
Penor 02 studied under Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and also taught both Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Penor Rinpoche (1933–2009) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Palyul Monastery and under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche (~1960–1991), founded the Ngagyur Nyingma Institute in 1978, and taught numerous students, including Jacob P. Dalton.

Pent Nurmekund (1906–1996) was an Estonian linguist and Indologist. He earned a Mag.fil. at the University of Tartu (1930–1935) under Friedrich Ernst Kieckers, studied at several European universities, and taught and conducted research at Tartu from 1955 to 1986.

Pentti Aalto (1917–1998) worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Helsinki under Gustaf John Ramstedt and Helmer Smith, and served as Docent at the University of Helsinki from 1949 to 1980.

Per Kjeld Sørensen (born 1950) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Erik Haarh at the University of Copenhagen. He was a lecturer at Copenhagen (1982–1989) and Professor at the University of Leipzig (1994–2017).

Per Kværne (born 1945) is a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned his Dr. phil. at the University of Oslo, taught at the University of Bergen (1970–1975), and was Secretary General of the IATS (~1989–1995).
Per Persson (1857–1929) was a linguist who studied at Uppsala University beginning in 1875. In 1895, he became Professor of Latin Language and Literature at Uppsala University.

Per Vilhelm Hilding Juliusson (1916–1977) was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Uppsala University (~1938–1944) and Stockholm University, completing a PhD under Åke Hultkrantz (~1970–1974).

Percy Brown (1872–1955) was an Indologist and art historian who studied at the Royal College of Art. He served as Principal of the National College of Arts (1899–1909) and later as Secretary and Curator of the Victoria Memorial (1927–1947).

Peri Bhaskararao (1947–2021) was an Indologist and linguist. He served as Professor of Phonetics and Phonology at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1977–1995) and held a post at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1995–2012).
Peri Sarveswara Sharma (1926–2000) was an Indologist and linguist. He completed his doctoral studies under Wilhelm Rau (~1968–1970) and held a post at the University of Marburg (~1972–1991).

Pero Slijepčević (1888–1964) was an Indologist who earned his PhD from the University of Fribourg (~1917–1920). He served as Professor of Germanistics at the University of Belgrade (~1927–1941) and the University of Sarajevo (~1950–1958).

Perry Link (born 1944) is a Sinologist who studied at Harvard University (~1962–1966). He taught Chinese language and literature at UCLA (1977–1988) and held the Chancellorial Chair Professor post at the University of California, Riverside (~2008).

Perry Schmidt-Leukel (born 1954) is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who completed his degrees at the University of Munich. He held professorships at the University of Glasgow (2000–2009) and the University of Münster (2009–2023).
Pertti Valtonen (1933–1999) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Helsinki (~1956–1964), where he also studied under Pentti Aalto (~1958–1968).
Petar Budmani (1835–1914) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Vienna in 1853. He served as a Professor at Dubrovnik Gymnasium from 1868 to 1882.

Peter Adamson (born 1972) is a philosopher and Indologist who studied at Williams College and the University of Notre Dame. He held posts at King's College London (~2000–2012) and the University of Munich (~2012).
